topic: Quantitative weighted recession gluing for honest polyhedral-label inference. For a fully encoded finite-label Gaussian experiment on an unbounded rational-polyhedral fan, prove effective compatibility-density: every globally honest near-minimizer admits a finite core and recession library whose Gaussian-weighted path discrepancies, chart errors, tails, and weight-variation remainders vanish with a computable input-dependent modulus. Build CertGluePFL, a terminating outward-rounded primal-dual algorithm with complete rational geometry, covariance, loss-scale, accuracy, Gaussian-integration, and bit-cost receipts. Prove fixed-stratum, moving-offset, and compact-exhaustion multinomial transfer, and instantiate survivor-complier ordered-wage quantile labels for the Chen--Flores Job Corps setting under M_ASC>=m_*>0. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Fresh presolve derived kernel-independent Gaussian smoothing error s^2 sqrt(d/8), tangential averaging error ||a||_1/T, weighted path and exact coverage-repair inequalities, and an explicit compatible recession representation. Exact rational checks gave contact risk 14/15, preserved four-label r=4 and nine-label r=6 strict gains, and improved the rigorous eta=.05,r=2 enclosure to 0.361100<=M<=0.813799. Destructive checks covered seam-centered means, oscillatory rules, metric rescaling, covariance encoding, escaping dual mass, recursion, moving offsets, and target positivity without finding a model-level counterexample or literature collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove simultaneous ECD across the full recession incidence diagram with an input-computable refinement modulus and then derive global certificate convergence and complete termination recurrences. EARLY KILL TEST: On the exact four-label eta=.05,r=2 fan, emit an executable honest primal and finite atomic dual with outward-rounded gap<=.001 after charging every chart, seam, protected-neighborhood integral, tail, covariance error, and repair; the current width is .452699. open_problems.open_problem: Can globally honest finite-label rules on a complete unbounded rational-polyhedral Gaussian fan be approximated by one incidence-compatible finite core and recession library, with a computable weighted-error modulus strong enough to yield a terminating outward-rounded primal-dual certificate?

source_refs.excerpt: No finite cover or uniform stopping level is claimed over the unbounded legal index set.

source_refs.claim: Computationally efficient near-optimal tests are constructed when each composite hypothesis is represented by a convex compact parameter set.
source_refs.author: Alexander Goldenshluger, Anatoli Juditsky, Arkadi Nemirovski

source_refs.claim: Cellwise recession cones need not form a fan; sufficient conditions and compatible subdivisions are given, but without a Gaussian approximation modulus.
source_refs.author: José Ignacio Burgos Gil, Martín Sombra

source_refs.claim: Dynamic programming approximates Gaussian integrals over possibly noncompact polytopes with explicit smoothing, truncation, and discretization errors.
source_refs.author: Morgan Jones, Matthew M. Peet
source_refs.venue: International Symposium on Mathematical Theory of Networks and Systems

source_refs.claim: Finite-sample optimal estimators and honest confidence intervals are derived for a causal ATE in a known-variance Gaussian model under convex restrictions.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesár

open_problems.why_unsolved: Prior CausalSmith work obtains only pointwise CAD density for a fixed semialgebraic input and explicitly lacks a finite cover or uniform stopping level on the unbounded index set. The web literature supplies separate ingredients: compact-convex Gaussian tests, qualitative recession-fan compatibility, and error-controlled Gaussian-polytope integration. It does not couple them into a simultaneous incidence-diagram refinement. Independently chosen recession charts can disagree on shared faces or around incidence cycles, while Gaussian weights vary along gluing paths and least-favorable dual mass can escape to infinity. The first missing proof step is therefore a single input-computable refinement modulus controlling weighted path discrepancy, chart approximation, seams, protected neighborhoods, covariance perturbation, and tails across every incident cone; the algorithmic step must then propagate those bounds through outward-rounded primal and atomic-dual programs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An effective compatibility-density theorem producing explicit core radius, rational chart mesh, compatible recession library, and error modulus from the encoded fan and tolerance, together with a CertGluePFL correctness and bit-complexity theorem whose outward-rounded primal and finite atomic-dual risks have certified gap at most ε and whose refinement recurrence always terminates.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation makes the practical cost of uniform honesty and executable finite-sample optimality part of the statistical problem before presenting the optimization machinery.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal conclusions require uniform coverage -> conventional tuning can violate honesty -> Gaussian structure permits finite-sample optimization -> causal label inference needs a certified analogue on an unbounded polyhedral fan.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the Minkowski-Weyl condition and extendable subdivisions to replace incompatible cellwise recession cones by a common conical complex, carrying the common-face proof through every incidence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A compatible recession library first requires exactly this common-face structure; the new theorem must make the subdivision quantitative and couple it to Gaussian weights.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert Gaussian-polytope integration into a finite-horizon Bellman recursion, smooth the discontinuous terminal cost, truncate the unbounded state space, and propagate sup-norm approximation errors recursively.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every certified primal and dual risk term is a Gaussian integral over a rational polyhedron, so this is the closest proof architecture for an explicit integration-error ledger.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce multiple composite decisions to pairwise affine detectors obtained from convex programs and prove risk control through exponential-moment saddle bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite labels induce finitely many pairwise errors; the missing extension is uniform control for noncompact fan cells plus a replayable dual lower-bound certificate.

open_problems.open_problem: Can certified Gaussian finite-label rules for causal partial-identification assertions be transferred quantitatively to multinomial experiments uniformly across fixed strata, moving offsets and active cones, and compact exhaustion?

source_refs.excerpt: Uniform sampled-data transport over moving full indices and active cones remains an open question

source_refs.claim: An explicit multinomial-to-normal deficiency bound is proved using recursive Markov kernels when cell probabilities are bounded away from zero.
source_refs.author: Andrew V. Carter

source_refs.claim: Calibrated projection yields uniformly valid confidence intervals for functions of partially identified parameters under drifting moment inequalities.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Exact minimum-average-volume confidence sets are constructed for multinomial probability vectors, although exact membership can be computationally difficult.
source_refs.author: Matthew L. Malloy, Ardhendu Tripathy, Robert D. Nowak
source_refs.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior proposal identifies the unresolved transfer over moving indices and active cones. Carter's comparison controls bounded-loss decisions over a fixed parameter set but assumes multinomial probabilities bounded away from zero; it does not track degenerating covariance charts, moving label offsets, discontinuous coverage indicators, or exhaustion of an unbounded local parameter space. Weak convergence alone does not preserve an unbounded risk criterion, and additive comparison error can dominate protected seam probabilities. The first missing step is a family of parameter-independent forward and reverse comparison kernels, or equally explicit direct risk couplings, whose boundary, covariance, and tail errors remain uniform as offsets cross fan faces, followed by a uniform-integrability argument before compact exhaustion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A comparison theorem giving explicit uniform coverage and causal-label risk bounds between an implementable multinomial rule and its Gaussian-fan rule as functions of sample size, stratum masses, covariance conditioning, offset motion, seam probability, and exhaustion radius, with a corollary transferring honesty and ε-minimaxity.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats uniformity and computational feasibility as central requirements rather than afterthoughts when the active inequalities can change.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal identified sets induce projection questions -> active inequalities drift across data-generating sequences -> calibration restores uniform coverage -> certified Gaussian labels still require quantitative multinomial transfer across moving faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct parameter-independent recursive Markov kernels between multinomial and Gaussian experiments and bound their total-variation errors using binomial local-limit estimates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Deficiency transports all bounded finite-label losses directly; the new proof must localize the kernel argument to changing strata and add moving-boundary and tail control.

method_exemplars.technique: Index drifting-strength subsequences and prove uniform stochastic expansions separately across weak, semi-strong, and strong regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Moving offsets and active cones generate an analogous family of local regimes that a fixed-stratum Gaussian limit does not exhaust.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact multinomial tests to obtain finite-sample valid regions and project them to target functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The exact discrete construction supplies a small-sample honesty benchmark and a possible coverage-repair device for the transferred Gaussian rule.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the finite binary-IV survivor-complier model admit a constructive legal inner-neighborhood theorem realizing every capacity-envelope direction needed for benefit-bound inference by nearby admissible multinomial laws, including zero cells and simultaneous cut ties?

source_refs.excerpt: The unresolved mathematical core is a legal observed-law inner-neighborhood comparison
add a checkable facewise sufficient condition for the legal tangent lift

open_problems.why_unsolved: The convenient capacity envelope is defined on an ambient probability vector, but nonnegativity, normalization, binary-IV compatibility, treatment monotonicity, and survivor restrictions make the observable-law image smaller. At zero cells the true tangent cone may exclude ambient directions that maximize an endpoint, while tied cuts require several directions to be realized by one nearby legal law. Algebraic totalization outside the legal domain does not prove such a lift. The missing construction must perturb latent allocations, preserve every causal restriction, and prove that their observable derivatives dominate all endpoint-relevant ambient directions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite facewise criterion and constructive map from each endpoint-relevant envelope direction to an admissible O(t)-nearby binary-IV law, proving two-sided derivative domination uniformly over laws with survivor-complier mass at least m_* or furnishing an explicit finite-support counterexample.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation keeps the legal causal data-generating-process region, rather than an unconstrained probability vector, central to discrete sharp-bound analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Discrete causal assumptions define a legal latent-law region -> sharp bounds optimize over that region -> ambient perturbations need not remain causally realizable -> characterize the legal local geometry required for uniform survivor-benefit inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate partial-identification regularity into tangent-cone and constraint-qualification statements, then compare feasible local-direction cones.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem is precisely a domination or equality relation between an ambient capacity cone and the genuine causal-law tangent cone.

method_exemplars.technique: Regularize inference for finite linear-program values while distinguishing fixed-law validity from the restrictions needed for uniformity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The survivor-benefit endpoints are finite optimization values, and the legal inner-neighborhood property is the model-specific condition needed for uniform inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a simultaneously honest, risk-minimax finite-label procedure for ordered survivor-complier wage-quantile assertions in the Job Corps experiment under the maintained lower bound M_ASC>=m_*>0?

source_refs.claim: Nonparametric average and quantile treatment-effect bounds under sample selection are estimated for Job Corps wages across quantiles and demographic groups.
source_refs.author: German Blanco, Carlos A. Flores, Alfonso Flores-Lagunes

source_refs.claim: Principal-stratum bounds address sample selection and noncompliance jointly for average Job Corps wage effects among always-employed compliers.
source_refs.author: Xuan Chen, Carlos A. Flores

source_refs.claim: Sharp bounds are derived for complier average and quantile treatment effects with noncompliance and truncation by death, without a sampling-inference theory.
source_refs.author: Kosuke Imai

source_refs.claim: Asymptotic inference is supplied for a survived-complier average effect, and the paper notes the limited estimator theory for earlier selection-plus-noncompliance bounds.
source_refs.author: Qinqing Liu, Xiang Peng, Tao Zhang, Yuhao Deng

open_problems.why_unsolved: The identification literature substantially occupies the scalar ingredients: Imai derives survivor-complier quantile bounds, Blanco–Flores–Flores-Lagunes estimate Job Corps wage-quantile bounds under selection, and Chen–Flores combine selection and noncompliance for average effects. More recent estimator theory remains mean-focused. These sources do not provide one jointly honest decision over several ordered quantile-bound assertions, handle intersections of their label boundaries, or optimize a finite-label loss. The first new step is to encode the quantile endpoints and ordering restrictions into one legal finite-label fan and prove that its Gaussian certificate and multinomial transfer remain uniform under the positive survivor-complier-mass condition.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully encoded multinomial rule and theorem that uniformly assigns one of finitely many ordered wage-quantile labels under the Chen–Flores/Imai model with M_ASC>=m_*, achieves simultaneous 1-α honesty, has a stated Gaussian-limit minimax risk and computable transfer modulus, and returns a certified Job Corps instance.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest application narrative, motivates wage quantiles through heterogeneous human-capital effects, and presents Job Corps conclusions in policy-readable quantile order.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Employment selection obscures wages -> partial identification avoids strong selection models -> quantile bounds reveal heterogeneous Job Corps effects -> policy reporting needs simultaneous honest labels for survivor-complier quantile assertions.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent truncation by death through contaminated outcome distributions, derive extremal trimmed CDFs, and invert them into sharp quantile-effect bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed labels are functions of these quantile-bound endpoints, whose active trimmed-CDF formulas determine the polyhedral chart boundaries.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate target-specific relaxations of moment inequalities and prove uniform bootstrap coverage for projections of partially identified parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest econometric template for uniform inference on functions of an estimated identified set, although the new object is a joint finite label rather than one scalar interval.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact multinomial p-values to construct finite-sample confidence regions and project them to target functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The Job Corps encoding is multinomial, making exact discrete coverage a natural small-sample benchmark and possible coverage-repair mechanism.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the jointly sharp identified set for survivor-complier ordinal benefit, no-harm, and large-gain probabilities when all coordinates must be realized by one common wage coupling and one compatible IV-selection completion?

source_refs.excerpt: Extend the attainment construction to a jointly sharp vector of benefit, no-harm, and large-gain tier events

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing work in the mined proposal proves sharp lower and upper values one event at a time, but the transport coupling attaining one threshold functional need not attain another. The Cartesian product of scalar intervals can therefore contain vectors that no common survivor-complier wage law realizes. New work must retain one coupling and one full IV-selection completion while projecting several overlapping staircase costs simultaneously; the scalar threshold-cut argument does not characterize all exposed faces of this joint image.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite facet, support-function, or multiobjective-transport characterization of the joint identified polytope for the three event probabilities, with compatible full-law attainment at every exposed boundary point and an estimator with a joint limit law or honest confidence region.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation centers on several ordinal measures of individual benefit and harm under incomplete causal information.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Mean effects conceal who benefits or is harmed -> ordinal outcomes define policy-relevant tier events -> partial identification yields eventwise bounds -> survivor-complier decisions require the jointly feasible vector of those events.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate ordinal causal events into staircase costs over couplings of potential-outcome marginals and derive sharp extremal formulas.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination has the same ordered-event geometry but must retain one coupling across several costs and unequal survivor-complier submargins.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent cross-world causal functionals as linear objectives over a common response-law or optimal-transport polytope and characterize projections through support functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The joint event vector is a linear projection of one feasible coupling polytope, so support functions can recover exposed faces without pasting incompatible scalar optimizers.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive inference for sharp distributional-treatment-effect bounds while accounting for nonsmooth estimated bound maps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The joint survivor-benefit polytope has estimated nonsmooth support functions and requires inference beyond separate plug-in endpoint intervals.

literature_map:
Goldenshluger, Juditsky, and Nemirovski (2015, EJS, arXiv:1311.6765) give efficient near-optimal affine-detector tests for multiple compact convex hypotheses.
Juditsky and Nemirovski (2016, EJS, arXiv:1604.02576) broaden detector machinery but lose blanket near-optimality outside favorable observation schemes.
Donoho (1994, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/aos/1176325367) relates Gaussian minimax risk to a modulus of continuity and optimal recovery.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, Econometrica, arXiv:1511.06028) and Armstrong and Kolesár (2021, Econometrica, arXiv:1712.04594) establish optimal honest Gaussian inference over convex regression classes and for causal ATEs.
Lee et al. (2016, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1311.6238) and Tibshirani et al. (2016, JASA, arXiv:1401.3889) obtain exact Gaussian inference after polyhedral selection through truncated-normal conditioning.
Kivaranovic and Leeb (2021, JASA, arXiv:1803.01665) show that standard polyhedral selective intervals can have infinite expected length, highlighting the statistical effect of unbounded faces.
Burgos Gil and Sombra (2011, DCG, arXiv:1008.2608) show that cellwise recession cones need not form a fan and give compatible-subdivision conditions.
Jones and Peet (2018, MTNS, arXiv:1802.02544) integrate Gaussians over possibly noncompact polytopes with explicit smoothing, truncation, and discretization bounds.
Cousins and Vempala (2018, SIAM Journal on Computing, arXiv:1409.6011) give randomized polynomial-time Gaussian-volume computation in an oracle/FPRAS model rather than an outward-rounded certificate model.
Carter (2002, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/aos/1028674839) bounds multinomial-Gaussian deficiency through explicit recursive kernels when cell probabilities are bounded away from zero.
Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2021, ISIT, arXiv:2002.01044) derive exact optimal multinomial confidence sets while noting difficult exact membership computation.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica, arXiv:1601.00934) give uniformly valid calibrated-projection inference for partially identified functions.
Imai (2008, Statistics & Probability Letters) and his 2007 noncompliance manuscript derive contaminated-distribution quantile bounds; Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes (2013, JHR) apply wage-quantile bounds to Job Corps.
Chen and Flores (2015, JBES) address Job Corps sample selection plus noncompliance for average always-employed-complier effects; Liu et al. (2024, arXiv:2405.16780) add mean-focused inference.
The targeted searches found the ingredients separately but no indexed theorem combining incidence-compatible recession gluing, a computable Gaussian-weighted modulus, outward-rounded primal-dual certification, moving-offset multinomial transfer, and survivor-complier quantile labels.
